subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should `cron run` be a permanently non-consuming operator operation that never changes one-shot consumption, retry/backoff counters, or scheduled next-run state, while only the timer and on-exit watcher retain scheduler-owned semantics?
rationale: This is a compatibility contract for existing operators and integrations, not a mechanical test-only choice; the patch intentionally changes manual-run semantics and introduces persisted attribution state.

options.title: Confirm operator-only semantics
options.body: Accept the public-contract direction after final-head live and upgrade proof demonstrates that timer and watcher-terminal behavior remain consuming.

options.title: Require an explicit destructive mode
options.body: Preserve current manual consumption behind an explicit, documented operator override if maintainers consider it a supported workflow.

options.title: Pause for a narrower contract
options.body: Hold the branch if the desired manual-run behavior or watcher boundary is not yet settled.

recommendation.title: Confirm operator-only semantics
recommendation.body: Accept the public-contract direction after final-head live and upgrade proof demonstrates that timer and watcher-terminal behavior remain consuming.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged cron scheduling work owns adjacent due-slot and maintenance invariants affected by this compatibility decision.
